decisions.reason: The candidate's existing message-35 INTRODUCE already captures the category label's placement before the author name and photo.
The source changes the placement of the collective author identity element, not the independently tracked size or shape of the author photo.
Category and author placement do not alter the Dorian Vale article's color restriction.
Using the website to determine article categories does not change the requirement to source article content from the website.
The category label is unrelated to the publication's issue date and edition metadata.
The article metadata placement decision does not change the deferred print-ready deliverable or its prepress settings.
The visually suitable category-label styling is already owned by the category-label requirement and does not modify the magazine-wide brand style.
Author and category placement within articles does not change the digital flipbook PDF deliverable.
The source does not change the requirement to enhance publication image quality when necessary.
Using the Flat Plan to determine categories is a category-label rule and does not change the existing general issue-assembly or Flat Plan structure requirement.
The source specifies article metadata placement but does not change the obligation to create a magazine layout template.
